title: [CQ-M03] Frozen matched workload corpus
description:
Objective: Freeze 20 representative starting snapshots and independent acceptance rubrics: maintenance, defects, refactors, non-routine changes.

Deliverable: Frozen matched workload corpus. This is task M03 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): M01.
definitionOfDone: Fixtures include reusable helper, stale positive/negative context, changed caller/requirements and recipe mismatch.
Each fixture names starting commit, intended behavior and independent assessment rubric.
Corpus can be reset without modifying the user working tree.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description: Tests first: after M03a-e dependencies are DONE/landed, read their actual workloadSnapshot contract/materializer and category exports before using them. Create matchedCorpus.test.ts asserting exactly twenty unique cases, five each maintenance/defect/refactor/non-routine, each rooted at full starting commit 35cf53c8444ebe1ca27e68bfbe8c5ca4896bac71 with explicit source/snapshot provenance, intended behavior and independent executable rubric. Pin concrete IDs and per-case/corpus digests from the landed datasets; require distinct task and starting contents, not cosmetic duplicates. Cover reusable-helper, stale-positive-context, stale-negative-context, changed-caller, changed-requirements and recipe-mismatch via actual fixture IDs and assertions. Reject duplicate/missing IDs, category imbalance, changed initial/assessment bytes or source provenance, malformed recipes and digest mismatches. Keep all category acceptance tests unchanged and do not author additional category cases here.
implementationPlan.note: Read the LANDED M03a contract (workloadSnapshot.ts: validateWorkloads, digestWorkload, digestFiles, createCodingSnapshot/createAssessmentSnapshot/readSnapshotFiles) and the four category exports (MAINTENANCE/DEFECT/REFACTOR/NON_ROUTINE_WORKLOADS) before writing tests. Created matchedCorpus.test.ts (corpus part): pins 20 ids in order, per-case digests (committed literals copied from the category tests) and a corpus digest computed by an independent standalone script from the documented encoding; coverage-tag -> fixture-id map, stale-artifact and argv-recipe checks, immutability, purity/import-allowlist guard, and rejection tests (missing/extra/imbalanced/miscategorized/duplicate/cosmetic/leaked/untagged/changed-bytes/rubric/provenance, malformed freeze, bounded ASCII messages). 'Malformed recipes' is interpreted as an assessment without an executable *.test.mjs plus the argv-data check on recipes/verify.json (the contract has no separate recipe field). RED confirmed in a fresh Linux scratch copy: the suite fails at import (matchedCorpus.js missing). Shared tree has 435 foreign dirty paths: untouched.

implementationPlan.description: Create matchedCorpus.ts as the frozen assembler over the real M03a-e exports, using the shared validator and canonical digest implementation instead of duplicating them. Introduce an explicit corpus version and committed literal freeze manifest: ordered twenty IDs, expected per-case digests and aggregate digest. Compare actual inputs to the freeze; never silently filter missing cases or recompute the expected baseline from changed data. Error handling must produce bounded actionable failures on malformed/missing/conflicting data or IO errors without dumping file contents/secrets. Keep original full startingCommit separate from fixture overlay bytes; label reduced/adapted snapshots honestly, never as exact full-repository archives. Export an immutable corpus for M04 without daemon startup, task/project mutation, model/network calls, prices or rollout controls. Preserve intended behavior/rubrics/recipes; coding inputs exclude held-out assessment/solution data. No production tool/schema or second revision authority.
implementationPlan.note: Created matchedCorpus.ts (276 lines): pure assembler over the real M03a-e exports using validateWorkloads/digestWorkload from M03a (no duplicated validator or digest). Exports MATCHED_CORPUS_VERSION=1, MATCHED_CORPUS_FIDELITY='reduced-fixture-overlay', CORPUS_FREEZE (committed literals: ordered 20 ids, per-case digests, corpus digest 9d0e42e6...), digestCorpus, assembleMatchedCorpus(sets, freeze=CORPUS_FREEZE), MATCHED_CORPUS. Order: validate freeze itself -> shape/5-per-category/category match -> cross-corpus distinctness (snapshot, assessment, intended behavior, cosmetic task copy) -> cross-case held-out leak -> coverage tags -> case-by-case compare to the freeze. Errors are bounded printable-ASCII invalidInput messages; the module does no IO. Gate in a fresh Linux git-archive scratch copy: matchedCorpus.test.ts 22/22, tsc --noEmit exit 0. DATA FINDING: the real data contains one pair of cases whose starting source is cosmetically identical (maintenance-usage-unknown-format and refactor-usage-counter-normalization differ only in header comment + one line wrap; assessments, intended behavior and rubric ids differ). A strict 'no cosmetic starting-content duplicate' rule would reject the landed, QA-approved producer data, which this task may not edit, so the cosmetic-copy invariant is keyed on starting contents AND assessments together, and the test pins that exact disclosed pair. Updated test regex accordingly.

implementationPlan.description: Complete corpus integration tests using the actual M03a materializer, not a second reset implementation: for each of twenty cases create two independent fresh temp snapshots, mutate one candidate, create a reset snapshot, and assert frozen starting bytes/digests are restored while the other snapshot, fixture objects and a separate user-working-tree sentinel stay unchanged. Assert coding snapshots exclude assessment files and correction/negative-control sources; independent assessments remain separately available to the later evaluator. Cover repeated/concurrent creation, spaces/Unicode, case/path collisions, symlinks and partial-IO cleanup with error handling confined to owned temporary handles. Never accept arbitrary destinations, remove repository roots, follow symlink targets, perform Git writes or write .moe. Category tests already prove unsolved/corrected/plausibly-wrong variants against unchanged rubrics; compose them unchanged rather than copy solutions. Recipes remain platform-declared argv data, not shell-interpolated code.

Create docs/matched-workload-corpus.md documenting the exact twenty IDs/categories, full base commit, source adaptations/representativeness limits, frozen digest encoding/version-update process and independent rubric boundary. Include a short example using the actual landed materialization/reset API and assembler for later M04, not invented helper names. Explain that matched arms use identical starting bytes and rubrics, reset creates only fresh owned temp snapshots, and assessments/solutions do not enter coding inputs. Use portable Node/path/temp examples for Windows/macOS/Linux, with no git checkout/reset/worktree recipe and no manual .moe edits. Missing future packet/revision/usage correlation is unknown, not zero overhead. Corpus validation is not baseline execution, model-quality evidence, VM isolation certification or rollout authorization. This narrow contract guide is needed by M04; M06 retains the epic-wide docs sweep.

One final verification gate: run exactly `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` fresh, require exit 0, and retain outputTail/test counts for complete_task. Existing Vitest src/**/*.test.ts discovery includes new tests without config/package edits. This full daemon command is required by M03 DoD, not a substitute for M06 system acceptance. In WSL use native Linux dependencies in a separate frozen source snapshot with unchanged package-lock/source hashes and Linux-only PATH; never overwrite Windows node_modules. Any scratch full-suite root must include docs, scripts, package scripts and root .gitignore because existing tests read them. Disclose unavailable platform runs, do not skip corpus cases, preserve all shared-tree/peer bytes and run no Git-write commands.

Final adversarial self-review (adversarial-self-review) of this three-file corpus assembly: could changed datasets redefine expected hashes, cosmetic copies satisfy twenty cases, unchanged/no-op solutions satisfy the intended-change criteria, stale-context/recipe cases be vacuous, or candidates see evaluator/solution data? Challenge digest encoding, immutable copies, malformed inputs, partial IO, parallel resets, symlink/path/case collisions and cleanup affecting user or peer files. Confirm no edits to producer modules/held-out tests, no daemon authority change, no production policy/verified-local activation and no benchmark/certification claims. If review fixes bytes/tests, rerun the same gate; complete_task reports fresh evidence and fixture provenance only.

This original M03 retains its original DoD and owns assembling/freezing exactly 20 from those dependencies, safe-reset integration and the mandated full daemon test command. No production or rollout change. Frozen starting source commit is 35cf53c8444ebe1ca27e68bfbe8c5ca4896bac71 (verified designated local branch HEAD); reduced/adapted source provenance must be labeled, not misrepresented as a whole-repository archive. Existing M06 remains the sole epic-wide integration/hardening gate. New category rows remain human-gated BACKLOG; no automatic status promotion.

planningNotes.risks: Frozen reduced/adapted sources must be labeled, never falsely presented as whole-repository snapshots or existing context API implementations. Independent executable assessments and red/corrected/wrong controls belong to category rows; parent must not weaken them. Expected freeze constants must not derive from changed fixtures at runtime. No evaluation leakage, source checkout writes, Git resets/writes, VM/model execution, price assumptions or readiness claims. Shared-tree foreign dirt and Windows dependencies require a complete frozen Linux test snapshot; do not modify source locks/dependencies. Required full daemon npm test remains the exact gate.
